headline: Helix Gene Therapy Trial Leaves 200 Children With Uncharted Mutations
body:
Internal documents obtained by the Lake Monitor confirm that Helix Biosystems' GenRenew Pediatric Program — marketed to low-income families in The Shelf and The Narrows as a preventive immune-enhancement therapy — has produced severe unintended genetic mutations in at least 212 children across four treatment cohorts between 2189 and 2191. The mutations, which Helix's own internal pathologists classify as 'expression anomalies outside all modeled parameters,' include accelerated cellular growth in peripheral nervous tissue, structural changes to ocular architecture, and in fourteen documented cases, the development of a secondary organ whose function has not been determined. Helix Biosystems has not issued a public statement.

'My son went in for what they told me was a routine immune boost. He came out with eyes that glow in the dark and fingers that won't stop growing,' said Darren Ekwueme-Solis, 38, of The Shelf, whose nine-year-old was enrolled in the program through a Helix community outreach clinic on Harrow Street. 'They told us it was free. There is no such thing as free from a corponation.' Forty-one families have now pulled their children from all Helix-affiliated medical facilities. The remaining families report they have been unable to disenroll due to ongoing 'monitoring requirements' listed in the program's original consent forms.

Dr. Astrid Nakamura-Bellows, a geneticist unaffiliated with Helix, reviewed a sample of the leaked documentation at this outlet's request. 'These are not modeling errors or acceptable variance,' she said. 'The therapy appears to have incorporated a second, undisclosed vector — something that was never in the published trial parameters. Someone added something, and someone approved it.' Helix Biosystems holds sovereign medical authority within its licensed districts, meaning Federal Remnant health regulators have no direct enforcement power without a formal jurisdictional challenge.

The Collective has established an emergency legal fund for affected families and is coordinating with Federal Remnant legislators on a challenge to Helix's territorial medical exemptions. Three Helix researchers named in the internal documents have not reported to work since the leak became known to company leadership on July 18th — their whereabouts are unknown.
aftermath: A Federal Remnant emergency health tribunal was convened in September 2191, but Helix successfully delayed all discovery proceedings through a series of jurisdictional appeals; as of this reporting, not one family has received compensation or a medical explanation.
runner_relevance: The Helix story generated some of the most ethically complex — and highest-paying — runner contracts of the early 2190s. Families hired runners to extract the three missing researchers before Helix could silence them permanently, making those targets among the most sought-after individuals in the city. Simultaneously, Helix was offering competing extraction contracts to find and return the same researchers under the language of 'employee welfare.' Data retrieval contracts focused on the undisclosed second therapy vector were circulating at 120,000 quanta or above. Courier runs moving evidence packages to Federal Remnant legislators through channels Helix couldn't monitor became critical, and protection details for the affected families — who reported increasing corporate surveillance — created steady ongoing work.
